concepts.title: Fluid Mosaic Model of the Plasma Membrane

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fluid Mosaic Model of the Plasma Membrane' refers to.
questions.a: Singer and Nicolson pictured the membrane in 1972 as a quasi-fluid phospholipid double layer - hydrophilic heads outward, hydrophobic tails inward - carrying a shifting mosaic of globular proteins that drift sideways through it.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fluid Mosaic Model of the Plasma Membrane'.
questions.a: A fluid lipid bilayer with drifting proteins explains why the cell boundary stays both flexible and selectively permeable.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Fluid Mosaic Model of the Plasma Membrane' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Transport Across the Plasma Membrane' refers to.
questions.a: Molecules cross the boundary three ways: passive drift down the gradient at zero energy cost (diffusion, osmosis), carrier- or channel-assisted passage for ions, glucose and amino acids, and uphill pumping that spends ATP or is coupled to a second gradient as symport or antiport.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Transport Across the Plasma Membrane'.
questions.a: Downhill moves free, assisted downhill is facilitated, uphill must be paid in ATP or borrowed from another gradient.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Transport Across the Plasma Membrane' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Cell Wall of Bacteria and Plants

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cell Wall of Bacteria and Plants' refers to.
questions.a: Many cells wear a rigid coat outside the membrane: peptidoglycan chains cross-linked by short peptides in bacteria (thick single-membrane layout in Gram-positive types, thin double-membrane layout in Gram-negative types), cellulose in most higher plants and chitin in fungi, with lignin hardening the secondary wall.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cell Wall of Bacteria and Plants'.
questions.a: The wall fixes shape and blocks osmotic bursting; several antibiotics kill bacteria by stopping peptidoglycan cross-linking.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Cell Wall of Bacteria and Plants' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Endomembrane System Compartments' refers to.
questions.a: A cooperating team of single-membrane organelles - rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, the Golgi stack with its cis receiving face and trans shipping face, lysosomes packed with acid hydrolases, and storage vacuoles - builds, modifies, packages and ships the cell's proteins and lipids.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Endomembrane System Compartments'.
questions.a: The secretory route runs rough ER to Golgi to vesicles to the cell surface, while lysosomes recycle damaged organelles by autophagy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Endomembrane System Compartments' taught, and from which source text?
